name: Filevine
summary: Case management for law firms: matters, intake, depositions, e-signature and AI document work.
best_for: law firms past the point where a general project tool works, with enough matters that case-specific workflows and intake tracking pay back a negotiated annual contract
skip_if: you are a small practice wanting a published price to compare — this category will not give you one, and simpler practice-management tools do publish theirs
honest_knock: Nothing is priced, so everything is negotiable — which cuts both ways. In legal software the number that usually surprises people is not the per-seat rate but implementation: data migration from your existing case system, template configuration and training, quoted separately and often as a one-off in the thousands. That figure is absent here along with everything else. Ask for it as its own line, ask what the contract length is, and ask what happens to your matter data if you leave. A custom quote is fine; a custom quote you cannot compare against a rate card is what you are trying to avoid.

pricing.notes: (2026-08-29 to 2026-10-06, read on their own pricing page) No prices are shown. Their own wording: all packages are custom built for your team's needs. The page describes five products — LOIS (AI features), Matters, Intake, Depositions and Signatures — and routes everything to a sales team for a custom quote. No per-user cost, no minimum seats, no contract length and no implementation fee is published, which is unchanged since 1 August 2026. What the page does name now is a free way in: LOIS Explore, described as a free tier of LOIS for AI-powered legal research and drafting, with a trial that takes no credit card.

compare_with.name: Clio or MyCase
compare_with.why: the standing comparison in legal case management — both publish per-user prices, which makes them the honest benchmark for whatever Filevine quotes

open_questions.question: Can you publish a price, or a starting price, for the plans that are quote-only?
Can a customer cancel at any time, and what happens to an annual plan that is cancelled mid-term?
Which data can a customer export, in which formats, on which plans?
Where is customer data stored, and can a customer choose the region?
Is there a minimum number of seats or users on any plan?
